newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end down, eyes on CS/Winterthur merger.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end down, eyes on CS/Winterthur merger.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower despite a spotlight on merger plans by bank concern Credit Suisse Group and insurer Winterthur, both of which ended lower.
Market reactions were mixed on the merger, which would produce one of the woreld's biggest financial services groups.
Dealers said some investors were unhappy about CS Group's planned capital increase and short-term profit dilution.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 39.2 points or 0.67 percent at 5,825.6.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) slid 22.82 points or 0.61 percent to 3,715.18 francs.
Bourse turnover reached 2.56 billion Swiss francs.
One dealer said the merger announcement could end a recent period of speculation in the Swiss financial sector which has boosted shares of various banks and insurers.
He added the market may see a correction in the next few days, depending on developments on Wall Street.
CS Group and Winterthur, which reached all-time highs in early trade, ended lower. CS Group was down 3.50 francs to 205 francs and Winterthur down 18 francs to 1,497 francs.

One trader also said the synergies of 300 million to 350 million Swiss francs that the companies have identified did not seem too impressive. Another dealer said the price of the deal was "quite high".
Other insurers profited from the planned merger.
Baloise, which has long been considered a takeover candidate, jumped 325 francs, or nearly nine percent, to 4,035 francs.
Insurer Zurich added 18 francs to 632. While some traders thought Zurich may deepen its cooperation with bank group SBC, others said this was unlikely.
Swiss Re was up 31 francs to 2,217.
Industrials were down on profit taking and the easing dollar. Novartis registered shares ended down 31 francs to 2,311.
